name: Webflow
tagline: Visual website builder and CMS for marketing sites

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked; 2026 public plan references list Basic monthly around $25/month, with lower annual pricing.

tiers.name: Site Starter
tiers.limits: Webflow.io subdomain; 2 static pages; 50 CMS items; 1 GB bandwidth; 50 form submissions total
tiers.notes: A free staging site; a custom domain requires a paid Site or Ecommerce plan.

tiers.name: Site Basic
tiers.limits: 1 custom-domain site; 300 static pages; no CMS; 10 GB bandwidth; unlimited form submissions

tiers.name: Site Premium
tiers.limits: 1 custom-domain site; 300 static pages; 20,000 CMS items; 40 CMS collections; 50 GB base bandwidth; unlimited forms
tiers.notes: Premium bandwidth add-ons are sold separately.

tiers.name: Platform Team
tiers.limits: Annual contract; 10 full seats included; up to 100 CMS collections, about 500 static pages and up to 30 TB bandwidth, plus enterprise workflow/localization controls
tiers.notes: Starts at $30,000/year; bundles platform, workspace and site capabilities.

tiers.name: Platform Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom traffic, seat, governance, security and service limits

tiers.name: Ecommerce Standard
tiers.limits: 500 ecommerce items; 2,000 CMS items; 50 GB bandwidth; 2% Webflow transaction fee
tiers.notes: Current annual effective price verified; the current first-party table did not expose a monthly-billing amount in accessible markup.

tiers.name: Ecommerce Plus
tiers.limits: 5,000 ecommerce items; up to 10,000 CMS items; 100 GB bandwidth; 0% Webflow transaction fee
tiers.notes: Current annual effective price verified; monthly-billing amount not exposed in accessible first-party markup.

tiers.name: Ecommerce Advanced
tiers.limits: 15,000 ecommerce items; up to 10,000 CMS items; 100 GB bandwidth; 0% Webflow transaction fee
tiers.notes: Current annual effective price verified; monthly-billing amount not exposed in accessible first-party markup.

tiers.name: Workspace Starter
tiers.limits: 2 staging sites; 2 pages/site; 50 CMS items/site; 200 AI credits; 1 full seat

tiers.name: Workspace Core
tiers.limits: 10 staging sites; 300 pages/site; 300 AI credits; 1 full seat included; code export and shared libraries
tiers.notes: Annual effective price; monthly amount was not exposed in the current accessible first-party table.

tiers.name: Workspace Growth

tiers.notes: Annual effective price; monthly amount was not exposed in the current accessible first-party table.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Site Starter: 2 pages, 50 CMS items, 1 GB bandwidth and 50 lifetime form submissions on a Webflow.io domain; free Workspace tiers include 1 full seat, 2 staging sites and 200 AI credits
pricing.billingTerms: free + monthly/annual Site billing; Workspace and Ecommerce annual effective prices shown, with some monthly amounts not publicly exposed in accessible markup; Platform Team is annual-contract-only
pricing.hiddenCosts: A paid Site/Ecommerce plan and a paid Workspace can stack; extra Full seats are $39/month and Limited seats $15/month when billed yearly; 2,000 extra AI credits cost $20/month yearly; premium bandwidth starts at $20/month yearly or $30 monthly per extra 50 GB; Localize, Optimize and Analyze are separate; Ecommerce Standard adds a 2% Webflow fee plus processor fees; repeated traffic surges can trigger an automatic upgrade

verdictSummary: A personal visual website builder is possible with existing editors, but Webflow's CMS, designer, hosting, animations, components, SEO, and client workflows are deep.
coreLoopDIY: Use a visual editor or generate static pages from blocks, publish to hosting, and add a small CMS.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because a designer can ship and maintain a production site without engineering every component.

priorArt.name: Webstudio
priorArt.desc: Open-source visual website builder and serious Webflow-like prior art.

alternatives.name: Concrete CMS
alternatives.desc: In-context page editing, blocks, collections and workflows; design freedom is more conventional.

facts.install: Release ZIP to PHP hosting, create a MySQL/MariaDB database, then finish the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Pages, users, settings and block data in SQL; uploaded assets in the server file manager or a configured remote storage location
facts.gapVsPaid: Concrete CMS's block-and-theme model offers far less precise visual CSS, animation and interaction control than Webflow.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP hosting, a database, writable directories, and responsibility for updates, backups and outbound mail

alternatives.name: Microweber
alternatives.desc: Drag-and-drop pages and CMS content in one PHP app; capable, quieter and decidedly self-hosted.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or upload the PHP package to a web host and complete its browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Site content and settings in a supported SQL database; images and other uploads in server storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Microweber cannot match Webflow's fine-grained visual CSS and interaction tooling, especially for complex responsive animation.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs compatible PHP extensions, URL rewriting, a database and correct filesystem permissions

alternatives.name: Plasmic
alternatives.desc: A hosted visual builder and CMS with custom domains free; the badge stays and the mental model leans React.

facts.install: Hosted signup; optional npm-installed Plasmic CLI for React code generation and deployment in your own repository
facts.engines: Plasmic AI (beta); the official site does not name its underlying model provider
facts.dataFormat: Hosted projects and CMS records in Plasmic Cloud; codegen writes React components plus plasmic.json and plasmic.lock into the user's repository
facts.gapVsPaid: Plasmic's component-and-code mental model is less direct for visual designers than Webflow's CSS-first designer, and free sites remain branded.
facts.setupBlocker: Free hosted output keeps Plasmic branding; codegen/self-deployment requires a Node/React project and deployment workflow

alternatives.name: Vvveb
alternatives.desc: A finished visual CMS with custom content, forms and publishing; less design polish, more PHP ownership.

facts.install: Download and upload the PHP release, open the site URL, and complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Content, products, orders and settings in MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite or PostgreSQL; media and downloadable files on the server filesystem
facts.gapVsPaid: Vvveb offers much less refined visual CSS, animation and interaction design than Webflow.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP hosting, a database, writable files, mail and payment configuration, plus ongoing server updates

alternatives.name: Webstudio
alternatives.desc: The closest honest replacement: visual CSS, reusable components and CMS data, with free custom domains only when self-hosted.

facts.install: Hosted signup or desktop app; alternatively export the project or deploy the self-hosted builder/site
facts.engines: Webstudio Inception AI and MCP integrations; the hosted model provider is not named in official documentation
facts.dataFormat: Projects and assets live in Webstudio Cloud when hosted there; export/self-host routes produce source or static assets under the user's deployment
facts.gapVsPaid: Webstudio's CMS and collaboration ecosystem is less mature, and its free custom-domain route requires running the deployment yourself.
facts.setupBlocker: The free cloud plan publishes only to a Webstudio subdomain; a free custom domain requires export or self-hosting

rejectedAlternatives.name: GrapesJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A framework for creating Webflow-like editors, not a visual CMS and hosting product.

notes: Strong kinda; plenty of prior art, but polish/client workflow is the moat.
prompt:
Build me a block-based marketing site generator to replace Webflow, for my own sites. Requirements:

- An Eleventy static site where a page is a YAML file listing blocks: hero, feature
  grid, testimonial, pricing table, FAQ, CTA, footer. Each block is a Nunjucks
  partial; building a page means editing YAML, not HTML.
- CMS collections without a CMS: blog posts and case studies as Markdown with front
  matter, listing and detail pages generated at build time.
- One design-tokens file (CSS custom properties for colors, type scale, spacing) so
  a restyle touches exactly one file.
- Responsive by default: every block works at 360px and 1280px, images via
  @11ty/eleventy-img.
- Forms POST to a small Express handler that emails me via SMTP creds in .env.
- Build to dist/, deploy with rsync to my VPS behind Caddy. Sitemap and per-page
  meta/OG tags generated at build.
- No accounts, no telemetry, content lives in git.
- Out of scope: a visual drag-and-drop designer and client handoff. If I truly need
  visual editing, self-host Webstudio instead of building an editor.
- README: block YAML reference with one full example page, DNS + Caddy snippet.
